provider: jsDelivr as the free CDN layer over GitHub repos

free_tier.stated: free with no limits on bandwidth or number of requests; GitHub-proxy soft limits of 10 000 actively accessed files and 100 000 files per repository
free_tier.notes: the file-count soft limits are not automatically enforced

per_object_cap.stated: files up to 20 MB through the GitHub proxy, regardless of repository size

retention.stated: | Immutable: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion' — deletion upstream does not remove it from jsDelivr

egress.terms: Unmetered, and immutable-cached at the edge: probed 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable' plus Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

tooling: URL pattern https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/USER/REPO@TAG/path — no client needed, no auth, no config. Purge API exists for cache busting.
chaining: Serving layer only: pair it with Releases (storage) or a git repo (small files). One repo backs 1 TiB/day because the edge absorbs repeats with a 1-year immutable TTL.
limits_note: Git repo files only — release assets are NOT served (probed: /gh/cli/cli@v2.102.1/dist/README.md -> 404). ~20 MB effective per-file ceiling for the GitHub proxy (the git-unlimited-storage README states 'jsDelivr per file | 20 MB'); hard per-file/per-package caps are undocumented and enforced at request time. Does not serve the >2 GiB release assets, so the serving path for big objects stays on GitHub's own Fastly edge.
reliability_note: Immutable: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion' — deletion upstream does not remove it from jsDelivr. Extension blocklist exists; binaries with unusual extensions can be refused.

evidence.proved: 'there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests'; soft limit '100 000' files per repository
probe: GET cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/jquery/jquery@3.7.1/dist/jquery.min.js -> 200, Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
jsDelivr CDN sets no limit on bandwidth or on the number of requests
evidence.quote: there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests

evidence.proved: the GitHub-proxy recommendation is at most 10 000 actively accessed files per repository
evidence.quote: We recommend that the number of actively accessed files per repository does not exceed 10 000.

evidence.proved: the GitHub-proxy soft limit is 100 000 files per repository
evidence.quote: The soft limit for the number of files per repository is 100 000.

evidence.proved: the soft limits are not automatically enforced
evidence.quote: These limits are not automatically enforced by us, but you agree not to exceed them.

evidence.proved: a jsDelivr member states the GitHub-proxy per-file limit of 20 MB
evidence.quote: We actually allow files up to 20 MB for GitHub regardless of the overall repo size

evidence.proved: served immutable files can outlive upstream deletion
evidence.quote: Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion.
